title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 82
paragraphs: It is also said that what follows was done. Xerxes in his flight from Greece had left to Mardonius the furnishings of his own tent. Pausanias, accordingly, seeing Mardonius's furnishings adorned with gold and silver and with hangings of different colors, ordered the bakers and cooks to prepare a meal as they were accustomed to do for Mardonius. When they did as commanded, it is said that Pausanias, seeing couches of gold and silver with luxurious coverings, tables of gold and silver, and the magnificent apparatus of the feast, was astonished at the good things set before him; and for sport he ordered his own servants to prepare a Laconian meal. When the banquet was served and the difference between the two was great, Pausanias laughed and sent for the Greek commanders; and when they had come together, Pausanias said, pointing to the preparation of the two meals: “Greeks, I assembled you for this reason — because I wished to show you the senselessness of this leader of the Medes, who, having such fare as this, came to us, who have such sorry fare as you see here, to take it away from us.” Thus Pausanias is said to have spoken to the Greek commanders.
